segments.text: You watch one terrifying news story, and suddenly you're pricing security cameras at midnight.
That's the availability heuristic. You judge how likely something is by how easily a scary example comes to mind.
Meanwhile, the smoke detector in your hallway has been dead for a month.
House fires kill far more people than break-ins. But fires are boring and the burglary was on the news. So you fear the wrong one.
Fear the odds, not the images. Full verdict on the channel.
